## ⭐ Second measured instance — and it is a **different line shape**, which widens this card

Triage seat (objectstack#6015), 2026-09-20T22:31Z. Found in the same unlock scan, on **objectui#8093**.

H19 reported that card's blocker as 「**1 of 1** … `#7434`」. The line it read:

> **Blocked-by:** PR **#8090** (the `AGENTS.md` half of objectui**#7434**, draft, awaiting human merge) · whatever PR repairs objectui**#8065** (the `skills/objectui` half)

⇒ the reader returned **`#7434`**, which appears on that line only as a **possessive** — 「objectui#7434's PR #8090」 — and dropped **both** real blockers (PR #8090 and #8065). Live-read this pass: PR #8090 **merged** 2026-09-07T03:49:35Z, #8065 **closed**. ⛔ #7434's own closure was never the condition.

### Why this is not just 「another one」

The first instance (objectui#8347) was **nine `·`-separated, backtick-decorated directives on one line** — a multiplicity failure. This one is **one directive whose remainder is prose containing three issue numbers**, and the reader picked the wrong one — not the first *directive*, but a number that is not a blocker at all.

⇒ two distinct failure modes under one heading:

| shape | what the line carries | what the reader returned |
|---|---|---|
| objectui#8347 | 9 directives, `·`-separated, each backticked | the 1st ⇒ **8 dropped** |
| objectui#8093 | 1 directive, prose remainder naming 3 numbers | **`#7434`** — a possessive, ⛔ not a blocker ⇒ **both real blockers dropped, and a false one substituted** |

⭐ The second is the worse of the two: dropping targets under-reads a block, but **substituting** one means H19's liveness answer is about an issue the card never waited on. On objectui#8093 the substitution happened to point at a closed card, so the row *looked* actionable — a release on it would have been right by accident, ⛔ not by reading.

### What this changes on this card

The pins here asked for N directives to yield N targets. ⚠️ That is necessary and ⛔ not sufficient. Add:

- a directive whose **remainder is prose** yields only the targets the **directive** names, ⛔ never a number that merely appears in the prose after it (the objectui#8093 shape: `Blocked-by: PR #8090 (the half of X#7434 …) · whatever PR repairs X#8065` ⇒ **#8090 and #8065**, ⛔ not #7434);
- a **PR number** is a legitimate target (PR #8090 was the real blocker here), so the fix must ⛔ not「repair」 this by filtering to issues only.

⚠️ And it sharpens the counting instruction already on this card: the census must classify by **line shape**, ⛔ not just count multi-target bodies — a body with one directive can be misread too, and those will not appear in a 「how many state multiple targets」 tally.

⛔ Still not claimed: the blast radius. Two instances, both found by hand, in one scan of a partial backlog.
